source.title: Perceptron capacity revisited: classification ability for correlated patterns

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: Tests random-label classification capacity for single-layer perceptrons, extending the subject to a different model class than the deep networks named in the claim.
record.gate_note: The study analyzes and reports results for single-layer perceptrons on randomly labeled patterns. These results do not test the claim versions as phrased for standard deep networks; recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study measures random-label classification capacity of single-layer perceptrons, not standard deep networks trained with stochastic gradient methods. None of its results tests V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors develop replica and TAP frameworks for correlated, randomly labeled perceptron patterns and demonstrate their validity and utility using one known result and two example problems.
record.recipe_differences: Statistical-mechanical replica and TAP analyses of single-layer perceptron classification capacity; no deep-network stochastic-gradient training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Extrapolated binary-weight perceptron capacities are approximately 0.819 for IID patterns and 0.938 for random orthogonal patterns.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-label classification capacity of binary-weight single-layer perceptrons depends on input-pattern structure.

fits_no_version.finding: Numerical estimates for spherical-weight perceptrons agree with capacity αc = 2c across the two tested nonzero eigenvalue spectra.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the studied pattern ensembles, spherical-weight perceptron capacity is determined by the input matrix's rank fraction c.

record.problems: The reported binary-weight capacity estimates use finite sizes N = 2, 3, . . . , 20; the authors describe the spherical-weight numerical estimates as based on extrapolation. The study does not measure deep-network training or test error.
record.rows_left_out: No study results were left out. Theoretical derivations and prior-work results were not entered as experimental rows.

untested.parts: Deep-network fitting of completely random labels with stochastic gradient methods, unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and chance test performance.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence as label corruption increases.
Deep-network fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across corrupted-label fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T3 classification contradicts its otherwise correct scope assessment. These are related capacity results outside all supplied versions, so discusses/T6 applies. Failure of the proposed message-passing algorithm to converge near α = 0.9 does not test V2.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests single-layer perceptrons, not standard deep networks or their architecture and training hyperparameters.
Does not compare training time or convergence across true and random labels.
Does not test shuffled pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs on deep networks.
Does not sweep corrupted-label fractions or report test error on deep networks.
Does not test these regularizers or generalization of deep networks.
Does not compare learning order for real and random labels.

rows.subject: simple perceptrons of binary weights
rows.operation_detail: Exhaustive search experiments estimated critical pattern ratio for randomly labeled IID patterns.
rows.note: The reported capacity estimates fit capacity for randomly labeled patterns, but do not measure training error or test error.
rows.check: The capacity estimate is correctly reported but concerns single-layer perceptrons. Capacity measures the existence of weights that classify every training pattern correctly; it does not establish SGD fitting by deep networks. Correct the experiment count from 106 to 10^6 and identify 0.819 as an extrapolated capacity estimate from finite sizes.

rows.subject: simple perceptrons of binary weights
rows.operation_detail: Exhaustive search experiments estimated critical pattern ratio for random orthogonal patterns.
rows.note: The authors state this is reasonably close to the theoretical prediction 0.940; capacity is not the claim versions' training-error and test-error measure.
rows.check: The capacity estimate is correctly reported but concerns single-layer perceptrons and exhaustive weight search. Correct the experiment count from 106 to 10^6 and identify 0.938 as an extrapolated capacity estimate from finite sizes.

rows.subject: simple perceptron with spherical weights
rows.operation_detail: Numerical experiments assessed critical pattern ratio for rank-deficient pattern matrices.
rows.value: The estimates of αc show excellent consistency with the theoretical prediction αc = 2c regardless of ρ̃(λ).
rows.note: The result concerns perceptron capacity for random labels, not the deep-network measures in the claim versions.
rows.check: The result concerns single-layer perceptrons. Figure 2 uses 10^4 experiments, extrapolates perceptron-learning convergence thresholds over update limits, and then extrapolates across finite sizes. Capacity concerns perfect classification feasibility, but cannot establish any deep-network claim version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
